name: Pharaoh and Abimelech, who took Sarah
charge: Taking another man's wife into the king's house
summary: Twice Abraham called Sarah his sister, and twice a king took her. Pharaoh's household was plagued; Abimelech was warned in a dream and required to restore her. God expressly testified that he had kept Abimelech from touching her. The marriage stood despite the account given of it.
offense: In Egypt, Pharaoh's princes commended Sarai and she was taken into Pharaoh's house (Genesis 12:15). In Gerar, Abimelech sent and took Sarah (Genesis 20:2). Both acted on Abraham's word that she was his sister, and Abimelech pleaded the integrity of his heart (Genesis 20:5); the Lord acknowledged his integrity and said that he had withheld him from sinning (Genesis 20:6). Yet Sarah remained another man's wife. Once that was revealed, Abimelech was required to restore her; ignorance was not permission to keep her.
judgment: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai. To Abimelech he came in a dream: thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. The Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech, and opened them only when Sarah was restored and Abraham, the prophet, prayed for him.

entries.commentary: The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred, and from his father's house. He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go. Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa.
Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.

God came to Abimelech in a dream: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before [Exodus 20:14](/bible/exodus/20#v14); the Most High said, I withheld thee from sinning against me. Abimelech had acted in the integrity of his heart, and the Most High withheld him from touching her. Restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee.

Abimelech called it what it is: a great sin. Adultery is one of the weightier matters; there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it. Abraham thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place. And technically she was his sister: the daughter of his father but not of his mother, who became his wife; the sister saying was their agreement in every strange land.

Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah; when Abraham prayed, God healed them. The same happened with Pharaoh before. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet's wife; He does not play about that.

Give thanks unto the Most High, call upon His name, and make known His deeds among the people. Sing unto Him, glory in His holy name, and let the heart of them that seek Him rejoice; seek His face forevermore. Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past. -

O seed of Abraham and children of Jacob His chosen: the Most High is our God and His judgments are in all the earth. He has remembered His covenant forever, the word commanded to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, confirmed to Jacob for a law and to Israel for an everlasting covenant. If Israel was to have an everlasting covenant, then the new covenant cannot suddenly involve all people. You must ask these questions of anyone who does not use the scriptures.

When they were few and strangers in the land, He suffered no man to wrong them and reproved kings for their sake: touch not mine anointed. He called a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant and bound with fetters until his word came to pass. The king loosed him and made him lord of his house and ruler of his substance, to bind his princes and teach his senators wisdom. Our forefather Joseph taught the Egyptians; those who boast in Egyptology forget our forefathers taught them. -

Israel came into Egypt and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham; He increased His people and made them stronger than their enemies, then turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate them. He sent Moses and Aaron who showed His signs and wonders in the land of Ham; He recounts the plagues of darkness, blood, frogs, flies, lice, hail, fire, and locusts. The locusts and caterpillars devoured all the herbs and fruit of the ground; this is the devourer, and the Most High promises to rebuke the devourer for the sake of a righteous nation. He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it. -

He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among the tribes; look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses. He spread a cloud for a covering and fire for light, brought quails and the bread of heaven, and opened the rock so the waters gushed out in the dry place. He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America. -

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair.
The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
And he entreated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he asses, and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.
And the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.
And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?
Why saidst thou, She is my sister? so I might have taken her to me to wife: now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him: and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that he had.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toward the south country, and dwelled between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman which thou hast taken; for she is a man’s wife.
But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, wilt thou slay also a righteous nation?
Said he not unto me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands have I done this.
And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

Now therefore restore the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore her not, know thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that are thine.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and womenservants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.

And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is to thee a covering of the eyes, unto all that are with thee, and with all other: thus she was reproved.
So Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bare children.
For the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s wife.
When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people;
He suffered no man to do them wrong: yea, he reproved kings for their sakes;
Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
